article_title: Automated Recommendation of Programming Learning Content Using Pattern-based Knowledge Components
citation: Muntasir Hoq, Griffin Pitts, Zhangqi Duan, Arun Balajiee Lekshmi Narayanan, Mohammad Hassany, Andrew Lan, Peter Brusilovsky and Bita Akram. (2026). Automated Recommendation of Programming Learning Content Using Pattern-based Knowledge Components. CSEDM'26: 10th Educational Data Mining in Computer Science Education Workshop. https://educationaldatamining.org
title: PCEX expert-bundled Python dataset
description: The evaluation corpus comes from the PCEX system, which "provides online access to worked code examples and short code completion tasks". It contains 123 programs spanning 13 topics such as Variables and Operations, If–Else, Boolean Expressions, For Loops, and Nested Loops, partitioned into 49 bundles of roughly one worked example plus one to three related challenges (average 1.35 challenges per bundle). Expert topic and bundle assignments serve as gold-standard labels for retrieval and clustering evaluation.
requirements: Constructing such bundles is time- and expertise-intensive, which the authors state motivates automated approaches
target_learning_goals: practicing programming concepts with conceptually aligned examples and challenges
examples: Prior studies validated the expert-defined bundles, and Figures 1a-1c illustrate same-bundle and different-bundle code within the For Loops topic
key_sources: Muntasir Hoq, Griffin Pitts, Zhangqi Duan, Arun Balajiee Lekshmi Narayanan, Mohammad Hassany, Andrew Lan, Peter Brusilovsky and Bita Akram. (2026). Automated Recommendation of Programming Learning Content Using Pattern-based Knowledge Components. CSEDM'26: 10th Educational Data Mining in Computer Science Education Workshop. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.05409

article_title: Gaze awareness and metacognitive suggestions by a pedagogical conversational agent: an experimental investigation on interventions to support collaborative learning process and performance
citation: Hayashi, Y. (2020). Gaze awareness and metacognitive suggestions by a pedagogical conversational agent: an experimental investigation on interventions to support collaborative learning process and performance. International Journal of Computer-Supported Collaborative Learning. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11412-020-09333-3
title: PCA with five types of metacognitive suggestion delivered during dyadic explanation
description: The study used a pedagogical conversational agent (PCA) installed on a server that automatically analyzed learners' word types to determine whether explanations were effective, with a rule-based generator selecting prompts from five types: "Metacognitive suggestion", "facilitation of knowledge integration" (perspective-taking and turn-switching prompts), and "Communication encouragement" including motivational remarks and focus prompts. Suggestions were triggered by keyword detection and delivered verbally in speech lasting an average of three seconds, with a text version presented under the agent image.
requirements: A server-client network platform that transcribes learner speech for keyword detection and delivers prompts at conversation gaps.
Rule-based keyword lists distinguishing efficient explanations (e.g., key task terms) from non-efficient ones (e.g., give-up phrases).
constraints: Suggestions were executed by an experimenter signaling during a momentary gap, capped at a maximum of 10 presentations per task and one per minute.
The technical-coordination process code was excluded because no technical issues arose in this task.
target_learners: Freshman and sophomore psychology students working in same-gender dyads
target_learning_goals: Explaining technical cognitive-science concepts to a partner and integrating two concepts into one topic understanding
examples: Type A example printed: "Please remember that the task is to explain the topic using the two concepts."; Type D motivational remarks such as "Good job! Keep going!"
key_sources: Hayashi, Y. (2020). Gaze awareness and metacognitive suggestions by a pedagogical conversational agent: an experimental investigation on interventions to support collaborative learning process and performance. International Journal of Computer-Supported Collaborative Learning. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11412-020-09333-3

article_title: Pedagogical content knowledge and content knowledge of secondary mathematics teachers.
citation: Krauss, Stefan; Brunner, M.; Kunter, M.; Baumert, J.; Blum, W.; Neubrand, M.; Jordan, A. (2008). Pedagogical content knowledge and content knowledge of secondary mathematics teachers. Journal of Educational Psychology 100 (3), S. 716-725. https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-0663.100.3.716
title: Shulman-based conceptualization of PCK and CK as distinct knowledge categories of secondary mathematics teachers
description: The article presents a conceptualization, drawing on Shulman (1986), of two teacher knowledge categories: pedagogical content knowledge and content knowledge of secondary-level mathematics teachers. The authors state they "present a conceptualization of the pedagogical content knowledge and content knowledge of secondary-level mathematics teachers" and describe "the theory-based construction of tests to assess these knowledge categories." The framework organizes teacher professional knowledge into these two distinguishable categories and grounds their measurement in theory.
requirements: Theory-based test construction to operationalize the two knowledge categories
target_learning_goals: pedagogical content knowledge
content knowledge in mathematics
examples: Tests constructed on this conceptualization were implemented with German mathematics teachers (N=198)
key_sources: Krauss, Stefan; Brunner, M.; Kunter, M.; Baumert, J.; Blum, W.; Neubrand, M.; Jordan, A. (2008). Pedagogical content knowledge and content knowledge of secondary mathematics teachers. Journal of Educational Psychology 100 (3), S. 716-725. https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-0663.100.3.716

article_title: Pedagogical content knowledge and content knowledge of secondary mathematics teachers.
citation: Krauss, Stefan; Brunner, M.; Kunter, M.; Baumert, J.; Blum, W.; Neubrand, M.; Jordan, A. (2008). Pedagogical content knowledge and content knowledge of secondary mathematics teachers. Journal of Educational Psychology 100 (3), S. 716-725. https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-0663.100.3.716
title: Theory-based tests assessing PCK and CK of secondary mathematics teachers
description: An assessment instrument pair built to measure pedagogical content knowledge and content knowledge of secondary mathematics teachers. The article describes "the theory-based construction of tests to assess these knowledge categories and the implementation of these tests in a sample of German mathematics teachers (N=198)." The tests served to examine whether the two knowledge categories can be distinguished empirically and how their connectedness varies with mathematical expertise.
requirements: Grounding in the Shulman-based conceptualization of the two knowledge categories
target_learning_goals: measuring teacher pedagogical content knowledge
measuring teacher content knowledge
examples: Implemented in a sample of German mathematics teachers (N=198)
key_sources: Krauss, Stefan; Brunner, M.; Kunter, M.; Baumert, J.; Blum, W.; Neubrand, M.; Jordan, A. (2008). Pedagogical content knowledge and content knowledge of secondary mathematics teachers. Journal of Educational Psychology 100 (3), S. 716-725. https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-0663.100.3.716

article_title: The Guiding Effects of a Critical Reading Program on the Use of External Reading Strategies When Confronting an Ironical Text
citation: Aysegul Karabay. (2015). The guiding effects of a critical reading program on the use of external reading strategies when confronting an ironical text. Educational Research and Reviews. https://doi.org/10.5897/ERR2015.2419
title: Program of Critical Reading Instruction (PCRI), a three-stage critical reading program from Goatly (2000)
description: PCRI is the instructional program implemented in the experimental group, drawn from Goatly (2000) and delivered over 18 course hours arranged as a three-hour course structure. The article describes it as consisting of three stages: "'Code Declination and the Description of the Text (What is meant in the text?)'", interpretation and inference of the text, and determining "'The Ideology behind the first and second stages and the Determination of the Explanations'". Instruction was conducted mostly through the program's critical reading activities.
requirements: Delivered as an 18-course-hour program implemented by an instructor, with instruction oriented around the program's critical reading activities
constraints: The article states the research is limited to the effects of PCRI on pre-service teachers' critical reading and the external strategies they used while reading
target_learners: Undergraduate pre-service teachers in Elementary Education
target_learning_goals: Critical reading of ironical texts
Use of external reading strategies such as note-taking and underlining
examples: The researcher implemented PCRI in the experimental group while a related instructor implemented the existing program in the control group
key_sources: Aysegul Karabay. (2015). The guiding effects of a critical reading program on the use of external reading strategies when confronting an ironical text. Educational Research and Reviews. https://doi.org/10.5897/ERR2015.2419

article_title: Implementing Argumentation-Based Science Learning Approach in Social Studies: Academic Achievement and Students' Views
citation: Akbaş, Y.; Şahin, İ. F.; Meral, E. (2019). Implementing Argumentation-Based Science Learning Approach in Social Studies: Academic Achievement and Students' Views. Review of International Geographical Education Online (RIGEO), 9(1), 209-245. https://doi.org/10.33403/rigeo.529139
title: Population in our Country Academic Achievement Test (PCAAT)
description: The PCAAT is a researcher-developed, 30-question four-choice multiple-choice achievement test measuring learning outcomes of the seventh-grade "Population in Country" unit, built from a table of specifications and Bloom Taxonomy cognitive steps. Items were retained with "item discrimination index of .30 or higher and the item difficulty index between .40 and .69" after piloting with 96 eighth-grade students. The final form's average item difficulty index was .51 and the KR-20 reliability coefficient was .78.
requirements: Administered as pre- and post-test around the implementation to measure academic achievement change
constraints: Valid only for the targeted Population in Our Country unit outcomes of the Turkish seventh-grade social studies curriculum
target_learning_goals: population geography content knowledge in social studies
examples: Item analysis with the TestAn program excluded items with discrimination index .19 and below and difficulty index below .40 before finalizing 30 questions
key_sources: Akbaş, Y.; Şahin, İ. F.; Meral, E. (2019). Implementing Argumentation-Based Science Learning Approach in Social Studies: Academic Achievement and Students' Views. Review of International Geographical Education Online (RIGEO), 9(1), 209-245. https://doi.org/10.33403/rigeo.529139

article_title: Family-Based Training Program Improves Brain Function, Cognition, and Behavior in Lower Socioeconomic Status Preschoolers
citation: Pakulak, E., Stevens, C., Bell, T. A., Fanning, J., Klein, S., Isbell, E., & Neville, H. (2013). Family-based training program improves brain function, cognition, and behavior in lower socioeconomic status preschoolers. SREE Fall 2013 Conference Abstract. https://www.sree.org
title: Parents and Children Making Connections: Highlighting Attention (PCMC-A)
description: PCMC-A is an eight-week, family-based training program with a child-directed component and a family-based, parent-directed component. The child component used "a set of 20 small group activities (4-6 children: 2 adults)" targeting vigilance, selective attention, task switching, and self-regulation of attention and emotion. The parent component adapted the evidence-based LIFT curriculum into "a scaffolded set of 25 strategies delivered in small group format," supplemented by weekly support calls confirming home-practice implementation.
requirements: Parents attend eight weekly two-hour small-group classes at Head Start sites with concurrent child small-group training activities
Weekly support calls to confirm correct implementation of home-practice activities
constraints: Developed and tested with lower SES, monolingual English-speaking Head Start families living at or below the poverty level; children with psychoactive medication use or diagnosed behavioral or neurological syndromes were excluded
target_learners: 3-5 year-old lower SES Head Start children and their parents
target_learning_goals: Selective attention and self-regulation of attention and emotion
Academic readiness
Parenting practices supporting family stress regulation, contingency-based discipline, responsiveness, and child attention
examples: Children completed two to four of the 20 activities per small-group session; parents of 4-6 children met with one interventionist
key_sources: Pakulak, E., Stevens, C., Bell, T. A., Fanning, J., Klein, S., Isbell, E., & Neville, H. (2013). Family-based training program improves brain function, cognition, and behavior in lower socioeconomic status preschoolers. SREE Fall 2013 Conference Abstract. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED563293

article_title: Enhancing Thai Engineering Students' Complaints and Apologies through Pragmatic Consciousness-Raising Approach (PCR)
citation: Uraiwan Rattanapan Noonkong, Anamai Damnet, Kanjana Charttrakul. (2017). Enhancing Thai Engineering Students’ Complaints and Apologies through Pragmatic Consciousness-Raising Approach (PCR). Advances in Language and Literary Studies. https://doi.org/10.7575/aiac.alls.v.8n.6p.92
title: Pragmatic Consciousness-Raising (PCR) model: a two-level noticing-then-understanding route from attention to intake
description: The article presents a PCR model adapted from Schmidt's Noticing Hypothesis, Ishihara & Cohen (2010), and Leech's General Pragmatics, in which pragmatic learning proceeds through two levels. In the article's words, "During the noticing phase, learners are exposed to native speakers' use of language through the discussion of the forms and grammar as well as the impacts of contextual factors." A second level of understanding realizes principles, rules, and patterns of expressions and the influences of social factors through interaction, after which noticed input may become intake and be used in real interaction.
requirements: Learners must consciously attend to pragmatic information such as forms, functional meaning, and relevant contextual features for pragmatic learning to occur
constraints: The article notes learners apply the pragmatic norms in other settings when their English proficiency develops
target_learners: third and fourth year Thai EFL engineering students
target_learning_goals: pragmalinguistic and sociopragmatic competence in complaints and apologies
examples: The study's innovative class operationalized PCR through explicit teaching, worksheets, an L1/L2 comparison interview project, and WDCT and roleplay assessment
key_sources: Uraiwan Rattanapan Noonkong, Anamai Damnet, Kanjana Charttrakul. (2017). Enhancing Thai Engineering Students’ Complaints and Apologies through Pragmatic Consciousness-Raising Approach (PCR). Advances in Language and Literary Studies. https://doi.org/10.7575/aiac.alls.v.8n.6p.92

article_title: Enhancing Thai Engineering Students' Complaints and Apologies through Pragmatic Consciousness-Raising Approach (PCR)
citation: Uraiwan Rattanapan Noonkong, Anamai Damnet, Kanjana Charttrakul. (2017). Enhancing Thai Engineering Students’ Complaints and Apologies through Pragmatic Consciousness-Raising Approach (PCR). Advances in Language and Literary Studies. https://doi.org/10.7575/aiac.alls.v.8n.6p.92
title: Three-phase PCR lesson sequence combining deductive and inductive pragmatic instruction
description: The innovative class followed a three-phase session design embedded in an English for Communication course, with twelve sessions of three hours each. As the article states, "The diagram features three phases of the innovative classes, which include both deductive (teacher-provided pragmatic norms) and inductive instruction (learners' discovery of pragmatic norms)." Phase one was explicit teaching of complaint and apology strategies, phase two used worksheets and an interview project comparing Thai and native-speaker performance, and phase three was assessment through WDCTs and roleplay.
requirements: Baseline data on the most favorable native-speaker strategies to present during explicit teaching
constraints: The design was implemented in a single EFL course at one Rajamangala University of Technology with purposively sampled students
target_learners: third and fourth year engineering students in an EFL context
target_learning_goals: appropriate use of complaint and apology strategies across power and distance contexts
examples: Participants interviewed Thai and native speakers of English, administered a WDCT form to interviewees, and compared and contrasted the two groups' performances for the class
key_sources: Uraiwan Rattanapan Noonkong, Anamai Damnet, Kanjana Charttrakul. (2017). Enhancing Thai Engineering Students’ Complaints and Apologies through Pragmatic Consciousness-Raising Approach (PCR). Advances in Language and Literary Studies. https://doi.org/10.7575/aiac.alls.v.8n.6p.92

article_title: Prevention and Management of Percutaneous Coronary Intervention-Related Complications: Assessing the Impact of Simulation-Based Learning and Human Factors Training.
citation: Fukamizu Junichi et al. (2025). Prevention and Management of Percutaneous Coronary Intervention‐Related Complications: Assessing the Impact of Simulation‐Based Learning and Human Factors Training. Catheterization and Cardiovascular Interventions. https://doi.org/10.1002/ccd.70418
title: PCR–Terumo SBL program: six-scenario complication simulation with 3D silicon models and co-creative debriefing
description: A joint education program between EuroPCR and Terumo Corporation, running since 2018 with over 650 international physicians trained. Complications are "simulated using a 3-dimensional silicon model derived from CT cross-sectional imaging of normal human coronary, aortic, and great vessel anatomy". Six scenarios were designed from Japanese national surveillance data; 90-min sessions pair a 15-min introductory lecture with 65-min hands-on small-group work (3–5 participants with a simulation trainer) and a 10-min facilitated debriefing that lets small groups reach local consensus on algorithms and transfer learning to workplaces.
requirements: 3D silicon vascular models derived from CT imaging
Physician simulation trainer plus industry task-force support for small groups
Scenario selection informed by complication-frequency surveillance data
constraints: Sessions focus on one of three complications (stent loss, distal vessel perforation, mid-vessel perforation) at a time; scenario prioritization followed surveillance showing stent and guidewire-related incidents were the majority (70%) of data
target_learners: Interventional cardiologists attending an international cardiovascular intervention course
target_learning_goals: Prevention and bail-out management of PCI procedural complications
Non-technical skills and human-factors awareness in the cathlab team
examples: 2023–2024 EuroPCR sessions on stent loss, distal vessel perforation and mid-vessel perforation, with a type 3 perforation module piloted at EuroPCR 2024
key_sources: Fukamizu Junichi et al. (2025). Prevention and Management of Percutaneous Coronary Intervention‐Related Complications: Assessing the Impact of Simulation‐Based Learning and Human Factors Training. Catheterization and Cardiovascular Interventions. https://doi.org/10.1002/ccd.70418

article_title: Core competency in palliative care among intensive care unit nurses: A latent profile analysis.
citation: Guan Q, Zhu X, Xue Z, Peng M. (2025). Core competency in palliative care among intensive care unit nurses: A latent profile analysis. Nursing in Critical Care. https://doi.org/10.1111/nicc.70021
title: Palliative Care Nurses' Core Competences (PCNCC) scale: 28 items across four dimensions
description: The PCNCC scale, developed by Han, is the measurement instrument used to profile ICU nurses' palliative care core competency. It "includes 28 items across four dimensions: ethical care competency (7 items), physical and mental care competency (10 items), spiritual care competency (6 items) and self‐psychological adjustment competency (5 items)", each rated on a 5-point Likert scale from 'not capable' to 'very capable' for a total of 0–112, with higher scores indicating higher competency. In this study it had a Cronbach's alpha of .924 and served as the LPA indicator.
requirements: Respondents must rate capability on the 5-point Likert scale; the article used it with registered ICU nurses with at least one year of hospital work experience
constraints: Scores are self-reported; the article notes recall bias may exist in the online survey data
target_learning_goals: palliative care core competency assessment across ethical, physical and mental, spiritual, and self-psychological adjustment care
examples: Used as the continuous indicator for latent profile analysis in Mplus 8.3, yielding three competency profiles
key_sources: Guan Q, Zhu X, Xue Z, Peng M. (2025). Core competency in palliative care among intensive care unit nurses: A latent profile analysis. Nursing in Critical Care. https://doi.org/10.1111/nicc.70021

article_title: Reliability and validity of simulation-based Electrocardiogram assessment rubrics for cardiac life support skills among medical students using generalizability theory.
citation: Lertsakulbunlue, S., Thammasoon, K., & Kantiwong, A. (2025). Reliability and validity of simulation-based Electrocardiogram assessment rubrics for cardiac life support skills among medical students using generalizability theory. Medical Education Online, 30(1). https://doi.org/10.1080/10872981.2025.2479962
title: Simulation-based ACLS course with ten-item three-domain assessment rubric for pre-clinical medical students
description: The article describes an SBL course at Phramongkutklao College of Medicine integrating basic EKG interpretation into ACLS stations for 96 third-year pre-clinical students, using high-fidelity mannequins (Laerdal SimMan 3G and SimMom) across five stations, each with two raters. The ten-item assessment form "included three domains: (1) EKG and ACLS algorithm skills, (2) management and mechanisms of action, and (3) affective domains", with each item assigned a maximum score of 10 points. Students were assessed once as team leaders, worth 4% of the summative assessment.
requirements: Raters participated in a meeting to standardize the assessment process and understand the study objectives and form before use
Students completed pre-class briefing, e-learning assignments on EKG interpretation, and a lecture on pharmacological management before the SBL session
constraints: Due to limited time and resources, students attended the SBL class only once during the cardiovascular block
SBL is described as an expensive and resource-intensive learning method
target_learning_goals: Interpreting common EKGs within ACLS situations
Providing appropriate management based on the ACLS algorithm
Understanding mechanisms of action of pharmacological treatments used in the ACLS algorithm
examples: Each of the five stations presented two consecutive scenarios lasting about 30 minutes, with 5-minute briefing, 15-minute scenario engagement, and 10-minute debriefing
Each student was once assessed as a team leader and rotated through other roles within the ACLS team
key_sources: Lertsakulbunlue, S., Thammasoon, K., & Kantiwong, A. (2025). Reliability and validity of simulation-based Electrocardiogram assessment rubrics for cardiac life support skills among medical students using generalizability theory. Medical Education Online, 30(1). https://doi.org/10.1080/10872981.2025.2479962

article_title: Implementation and facilitation of post-resuscitation debriefing: a comparative crossover study of two post-resuscitation debriefing frameworks.
citation: Kam April J., Gonsalves Clarelle L., Nordlund Samantha V., Hale Stephen J., Twiss Jennifer, Cupido Cynthia, Brar Mandeep, Parker Melissa J. (2022). Implementation and facilitation of post-resuscitation debriefing: a comparative crossover study of two post-resuscitation debriefing frameworks. BMC Emergency Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12873-022-00707-4
title: PCP and DISCERN post-resuscitation debriefing tools
description: Two structured post-resuscitation debriefing tools implemented and compared in a pediatric tertiary care hospital. The article describes them as follows: "DISCERN is a more involved debriefing process that targets QI-type performance improvement, while PCP is a simpler process targeted more at the emotional well-being of care team members". Both are rooted in plus-delta principles; PCP adds questions on responder wellbeing and specific prompts on equipment and medications, while DISCERN uses broad open-ended questions (what went well, what could be improved).
requirements: A physical copy of the tool accessible at the point of care (attached to code carts or an envelope outside the resuscitation room), a trained debrief leader, and a scribe to record responses.
constraints: Neither tool was yet validated at the time of the study, per the article; DISCERN did not address team members' overall wellbeing and its broad questions sometimes yielded vague, non-descriptive answers.
target_learners: Interprofessional acute care teams in NICU, PICU, ED and Code Blue settings
target_learning_goals: Post-event reflection on team performance, identification of quality improvement opportunities, and emotional support of healthcare providers
examples: 59 PCP and 55 DISCERN debrief tools were completed over 12 months, each used to facilitate hot debriefings of five to 10 team members after triggering events.
key_sources: Kam April J., Gonsalves Clarelle L., Nordlund Samantha V., Hale Stephen J., Twiss Jennifer, Cupido Cynthia, Brar Mandeep, Parker Melissa J. (2022). Implementation and facilitation of post-resuscitation debriefing: a comparative crossover study of two post-resuscitation debriefing frameworks. BMC Emergency Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12873-022-00707-4
